## Five methods, five assumptions {#methods}

| Method | It assumes | It fails when |
|------|----------------|----------------|
| Drop the missing hours | The missing hours are like the others | Gaps follow a pattern, or the value caused them |
| Fill with the mean | Nothing changes over time | There is a daily cycle or a trend |
| Linear interpolation | The value moves steadily between its two neighbors | The gap is longer than the time the process takes to change |
| Carry the last value forward | Nothing changed since the last reading | The value moves; events appear late |
| Same hour on other days | Today follows the usual daily pattern | The day is unusual, or no other day has that hour |

[Every method is an assumption about the hours you did not measure. Choose the one whose assumption you can defend for this gap.]{.note-line}

## How long a gap can you bridge? {#bridge data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="bridgew" id="bridgew">
  <div class="sm-controls">
    <label class="sm-slider">Gap length, starting 11:00 on 28 April <strong id="bw-label">2 h</strong>
      <input type="range" id="bw-len" min="1" max="24" step="1" value="2">
    </label>
    <div class="sm-mode" role="group" aria-label="Fill method">
      <button type="button" data-m="linear" aria-pressed="true">Linear</button>
      <button type="button" data-m="hour" aria-pressed="false">Same hour</button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <svg id="bw-plot" viewBox="0 0 1160 300" role="img" aria-label="Three days of real benzene with a gap that grows from 11:00 on 28 April; the filled values are drawn over the true record"></svg>
  <div class="sm-readout" id="bw-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('bridgew'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  // Real benzene, µg/m³, 27 to 29 April 2004 (UCI Air Quality, reference analyzer), one value per hour.
  const Y = [2.2,1.7,1.6,1.5,2.5,3.3,8.9,23.4,23.8,7.9,8.2,8.8,14.6,18,12,14.8,12.5,15.5,17.7,21.6,18.9,12.5,8.8,10.9,
             8,4.4,2.8,2.7,2.2,2.5,7.5,30.4,22,24.7,18.4,16.8,14.2,15.7,21.9,20.8,16.2,19.8,28.9,28.3,24.9,13.1,8.6,9.5,
             7.8,5.2,2.8,2.3,2.5,4.4,9.4,29.8,36.2,18,10.9,9,14.4,22.3,20.9,23.1,21.2,24.8,28.6,32.6,19.2,16.3,13.7,13.6];
  // Mean of each hour of day over the other 13 days of the two-week window.
  const P = [6.91,5.19,3.37,3.16,2.65,3.35,6.47,15.42,17.35,12.3,9.34,9.12,10.41,11.65,10.85,11.68,10.8,13.46,15.78,16.98,13.35,10.08,8.5,8.52];
  const G0 = 35, N = Y.length;           // index 35 = 11:00 on 28 April
  let method = 'linear';
  const W = 1160, H = 300, L = 64, R = 16, T = 14, B = 44, top = 40;
  const X = (k) => L + (k / (N - 1)) * (W - L - R), V = (v) => T + (1 - v / top) * (H - T - B);
  function draw() {
    const len = +document.getElementById('bw-len').value, end = G0 + len - 1;
    document.getElementById('bw-label').textContent = len + ' h';
    const fill = Y.map((v, k) => k < G0 || k > end ? null
      : method === 'linear' ? Y[G0 - 1] + (Y[end + 1] - Y[G0 - 1]) * (k - G0 + 1) / (len + 1) : P[k % 24]);
    let g = '';
    for (const v of [0, 10, 20, 30, 40]) g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${V(v)}" y2="${V(v)}" stroke="#B9C1C6"/><text x="${L - 10}" y="${V(v) + 6}" text-anchor="end" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${v}</text>`;
    for (let d = 0; d < 3; d++) g += `<line x1="${X(d * 24)}" x2="${X(d * 24)}" y1="${H - B}" y2="${H - B + 6}" stroke="#333F4A"/><text x="${X(d * 24 + 12)}" y="${H - 14}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${27 + d} April</text>`;
    g += `<text transform="translate(18 ${(T + H - B) / 2}) rotate(-90)" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="#66727C">benzene, µg/m³</text>`;
    g += `<rect x="${X(G0) - 7}" y="${T}" width="${X(end) - X(G0) + 14}" height="${H - T - B}" fill="#DFC98F" opacity=".45"/>`;
    g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${L}" y1="${T}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${H - B}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="1.5"/>`;
    g += `<path d="${Y.map((v, k) => (k ? 'L' : 'M') + X(k).toFixed(1) + ',' + V(v).toFixed(1)).join('')}" fill="none" stroke="#0F6E6B" stroke-width="2"/>`;
    const seg = [G0 - 1, ...fill.map((v, k) => (v === null ? -1 : k)).filter((k) => k >= 0), end + 1];
    const yv = (k) => (fill[k] === null ? Y[k] : fill[k]);
    g += `<path d="${seg.map((k, i) => (i ? 'L' : 'M') + X(k).toFixed(1) + ',' + V(yv(k)).toFixed(1)).join('')}" fill="none" stroke="#E29A2D" stroke-width="3.5"/>`;
    document.getElementById('bw-plot').innerHTML = g;
    let worst = 0, sumT = 0, sumF = 0, peakT = -1, peakF = -1;
    for (let k = G0; k <= end; k++) { worst = Math.max(worst, Math.abs(fill[k] - Y[k])); sumT += Y[k]; sumF += fill[k]; peakT = Math.max(peakT, Y[k]); peakF = Math.max(peakF, fill[k]); }
    document.getElementById('bw-out').innerHTML = `<span class="sm-key"><i class="k-true"></i>true record <i class="k-rec"></i>filled</span>` +
      `<span class="sm-chip ${worst < 3 ? 'seen' : worst < 10 ? 'blurred' : 'missed'}">largest error in the gap: <b>${worst.toFixed(1)}</b></span>` +
      `<span class="sm-chip">highest hour in the gap: true <b>${peakT.toFixed(1)}</b>, filled <b>${peakF.toFixed(1)}</b></span>`;
  }
  document.getElementById('bw-len').addEventListener('input', draw);
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-m]').forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => {
    method = b.dataset.m; root.querySelectorAll('[data-m]').forEach((o) => o.setAttribute('aria-pressed', o === b)); draw();
  }));
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

[Real benzene, 27 to 29 April 2004 (Lab 02, Demo A). Data: De Vito, UCI Air Quality, doi:10.24432/C59K5F, CC BY 4.0.]{.source}

## Activity 1 · What the AI's fill hides {#act1 .activity}

[Pairs · 10 minutes · Lab 02, Step 4]{.act-label}

```{=html}
<pre class="code-slide"><span>df = pd.read_csv("benzene.csv", parse_dates=["datetime"])</span><span>df["C6H6_ugm3"] = df["C6H6_ugm3"].interpolate()</span><span>print(df["C6H6_ugm3"].isna().sum())   <b class="c"># 0: no gaps left</b></span><span>print(df["C6H6_ugm3"].mean())</span></pre>
```

::: {.prompt .small}
The code reports 0 missing values and a mean. What did it hide? Write the one sentence your report would need that this code cannot give you.
:::

::: {.selfstudy}
Studying alone: write your sentence, then go on.
:::

## What it hid {#act1-fix}

::: {.beforeafter}
::: {}
[What happened]{.label}
About 90 hours were invented. Across the three-day outage the line is straight: three nights and three rush hours are gone. The mean can look plausible while the typical daily peak (the mean of the daily maxima) is too low.
:::
::: {}
[A fill you can report]{.label}
Fill only short gaps, and count what you did.
:::
:::

```{=html}
<pre class="code-slide"><span>gap = s.isna().groupby(s.notna().cumsum()).transform("sum")</span><span>filled = s.fillna(s.interpolate(limit_area="inside").where(gap &lt;= 3))</span><span>print("filled:", (s.isna() &amp; filled.notna()).sum(), " still missing:", filled.isna().sum())</span></pre>
```

[Read it line by line: the first line measures each gap, the second fills only gaps of 3 hours or less, the third reports both counts.]{.note-line}

## Fill, flag, report {#rule}

::: {.why3}
::: {.w}
[1 · Fill]{.label}
**Only gaps that are short** compared with how fast the value changes. For benzene, which follows traffic, that is a few hours.
:::
::: {.w}
[2 · Flag]{.label}
**Keep a column that says which values were filled.** Later steps, such as a peak, a standard deviation or a count of exceedances, can then leave them out.
:::
::: {.w .hard}
[3 · Report]{.label}
**Next to the result:** hours measured, hours filled and by which method, hours still missing.
:::
:::

[A filled value is an estimate, not a measurement. The reader of your report must be able to tell the two apart.]{.note-line}
